note: File runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-153825-208b/answers.jsonl (present locally; otherwise fetched with modal volume get into runs/theory-tests/<job>/answers.jsonl). Row selection: attempt == 0, sample 0-3, first row per (problem_index, sample), then rows with cap_hit true or finish_reason 'length' dropped (after dedup, so a dropped cap hit is not replaced by a later duplicate). Right = score_v3 == 1, all other finished rows wrong. S = regex matches over the stored text, which for the base starts with the prefilled cue ' line!\n\nOkay' (cannot match the regex, so harmless); T = n_new. Main number is the pooled ratio over eligible problems; n = number of eligible problems (both groups span the same problems). Bootstrap over eligible problems; a resample with S_r == 0 gives +inf. Alt reading: macro average, mean over eligible problems of each problem's wrong rate divided by the mean of each problem's right rate. Refuted if R < 1.10 or S_r == 0 (refuted_without_number).

Files: base -208b and RL -e828 answers.jsonl (runs/theory-rows, fetched to runs/theory-tests if missing). Same row selection as p1, finished rows only, right and wrong together. Rate = pooled sum S / sum T per file; statistic = Rate(base)/Rate(RL). Bootstrap pairs the two files by problem_index (one tuple of base rows and RL rows per problem, union of problems). n = the smaller count of problems with a finished row (base or RL). If RL S sum is 0: +inf, not refuted (interval None), or refuted_without_number if base S is also 0. Alt reading: ratio of mean per-row rates (each row weighted equally). The RL file's text also begins with ' line!\n\nOkay' although the arm is 'plain'; text was used as stored. Refuted if statistic < 1.15.

File runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-183640-e828/answers.jsonl (RL plain). Identical code to p1 apart from the file and the refuted_by test (R > 1.40, or S_r == 0 -> refuted_without_number). RL has few finished-wrong rows (about 131 at attempt 0 before dedup), so the eligible set is small and the ratio may be noisy or dominated by a few long rows; n = eligible problems. Alt: macro-average ratio as in p1.

File base -208b. Same row selection as p1, all problems. Kept rows have exactly one SW match; p = match.start() in the stored text (which includes the 12-character cue prefix ' line!\n\nOkay', counted literally); short-final = (len(text) - p) < p. Statistic F_w - F_r. If either group has fewer than 10 rows: refuted_without_number. n = size of the smaller row group. Bootstrap over problems (each entry the problem's kept rows); in a resample an empty group's share is taken as 0. Alt reading: rows with at least one match, using the position of the last switch. A small one-switch wrong group makes the number noisy.
